---
title: "Lesson 8: Public vs. private repositories"
---

## The difference

| | **Public** | **Private** |
|---|---|---|
| Who can see it | **Anyone on the internet**, including search engines and automated scrapers | Only people you give access to |
| Who can edit it | Only people you give access to | Only people you give access to |
| Can others fork it? | Yes, anyone | Only members, and NV OSE has disabled this |
| GitHub Pages on the Free plan | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| Free security scanning | ✅ Full | Limited |

**Public means anyone can *see* it, not that anyone can *change* it.** Outsiders can only suggest changes, through forks and pull requests.

## What's public in a public repo

All of it:

- every file, **in every commit** in the history
- **every branch**, including work in progress
- issues, pull requests, comments, and commit messages
- the name and email on each commit (see email privacy in [Lesson 2](02-setup.qmd))

## Which to choose

| Choose **Public** for | Choose **Private** for |
|---|---|
| Training materials meant to be shared | Internal procedures and drafts |
| Code from published or approved analyses | Code from analyses that haven't been released or cleared |
| Templates and tools for other agencies | Anything that mentions internal systems, servers, or file paths |
| GitHub Pages websites | Anything you're unsure about |

::: {.callout-tip title="When in doubt, start private"}
A private repo can be made public later, after review. Making a public repo private doesn't erase what people have already seen, copied, or forked.
:::

## NV OSE repositories

| Repo | Visibility |
|---|---|
| `.github` (org profile and SOP) | Public |
| `training` | Public |
| `shared-resources` | Private |
| `presentations` | Private |
| `team-hub` | Private |

Only organization **owners** can change a repo's visibility. Ask an owner if you think a repo should be made public.

## Private ≠ safe for sensitive data

A private repo is still **not** an approved place for PHI, PII, or confidential data:

- Access can change when people join, leave, or are added by mistake.
- A repo can be made public by accident.
- Data in Git history is hard to remove completely.

See [Lesson 9](09-data-security.qmd).
